summary: Dieter Gunkel is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~2005–2010). He held posts at the University of Munich (2010–2017), the University of Richmond (2017–2024), and UCLA (2024).

Dieter Schlingloff studied at the University of Göttingen (Dr. phil. 1947–1952) under Ernst Waldschmidt and Humboldt University of Berlin (Habilitation, 1961). An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he held posts at Kiel, Göttingen, Munich, and Leipzig.
Dieter Schrapel is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (attested 1970) under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau.

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cologne (1963) under Shri Krishna Sharma and completed his PhD (1972) and Habilitation (~1972–1976) at the University of Bonn, where he was außerplanmäßiger Professor (1978–2007).

Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at Marburg, Munich, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD ~1956–1959). He served as Chair of the History of South Asia at Heidelberg University from 1968 to 2001.

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Pema Wangchok Gyelpo, later succeeding Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1987–1991).

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1959–1965). He held posts at Calcutta (1965–1977), Delhi (1977–1990), and the University of Cambridge (1990–2008) as Professor Emeritus of South Asian Archaeology.

Dilip Kumar Biswas was an Indologist and historian who studied at Presidency University (~1937–1941), the University of Calcutta (~1941–1943), and under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1948–1957) and Calcutta (~1957–1985).
Dilli Raman Regmi was a historian and Indologist who earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D. Litt. from Patna University (1961). He taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Dina Bangdel was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at Virginia Commonwealth University (~2002–2017) and Ohio State University (attested 2006).

Dines Andersen was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1879–1892) under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, later serving there as professor of Indian philology (1903–1927).

Dineschandra Sircar was an Indologist and historian. He was a lecturer (1937) and Carmichael Professor (1962) at the University of Calcutta, and served as Government Epigraphist for India with the Archaeological Survey of India (until 1961, attested 1987).

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.
Dipa Ma was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Anagarika Munindra (~1965–1969) and Mahasi Sayadaw (~1967–1969).
Dipak Kumar Barua is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Dean at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and was president of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1996–2004).

Dipak Ranjan Das is an Indologist and historian who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He held a post in the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Dipesh Chakrabarty is a historian and philosopher who studied at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD ~1977–1984 under Donald Anthony Low). He taught at Melbourne (~1985–1995) before becoming Distinguished Service Professor at Chicago (1995).

Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who studied at Leiden University (MA ~1956–1967, doctorate ~1975–1983). He held posts at the Kern Institute (1967, 1971–1991) and served as Chair of Indian History at Leiden (1991–2003).
Divyaraj Amiya is a scholar in Indology and linguistics with posts attested in 2026 as faculty at the University of Tübingen and as Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich.

Diwakar Acharya, an Indologist and philosopher, studied under Ramananda Giri and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (~2000–2004). He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, Hamburg, Kyoto University (2006–2016), and Oxford (professor from 2016).
